quote.text: If worldly things “be but as a dream, the thought is not far off that there may be an awakening to what is real. When he speaks of death as a necessary change, and points out that nothing useful and profitable can be brought about without change, did he perhaps think of the change in a corn of wheat, which is not quickened except it die? Nature’s marvellous power of recreating out of Corruption is surely not confined to bodily things.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Like the corn of wheat that must "die" in order to be reborn, parenting involves guiding a child through their inevitable challenges, fostering growth through transformation.
    • Embrace the constant changes in the family dynamic as opportunities for deeper learning and bond-building, understanding that every phase of growth paves the way for a richer understanding of life.
  • Leadership
    • Leadership is about steering through constant change—just as nature transforms corruption into new life, a good leader turns obstacles into opportunities for renewal and progress.
    • Recognize that change is not an end but a crucial step toward meaningful evolution, urging leaders to encourage innovation and foster team resilience amid transformation.
  • Product Management
    • In product management, the process of iterating and evolving mirrors nature’s cycles; discontinuing outdated models creates space for fresh, improved ideas to emerge.
    • This quote inspires product managers to view every change—even setbacks—as integral to the journey toward breakthroughs, encouraging a proactive embrace of uncertainty and innovation.
